claims.title: Unverified local client channel may expose player data to malware on the player device
claims.description: `flow:entity:player>process:game-client>launch-and-play` carries player input and game output on a local channel, while `encryption_in_transit` is unknown. If the local channel lacks an OS-enforced confidentiality boundary, malware or another unauthorized local principal controlling the player-owned host can read the exchange through `process:game-client`. This is conditional on the unverified transport/local-channel protection; it does not assert that local protection is absent. The disclosure can reveal player activity and any personal data present in the client interaction, enabling targeted account or social-engineering attempts against that player.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because `process:game-client` runs on hardware outside operator control and the local flow's protection is unknown; impact is low because the model identifies one player's `pii` rather than a shared corpus.

mitigations.detail: Use OS-scoped IPC and credential storage, avoid placing reusable secrets in client memory or local messages, and record the local protection posture for `flow:entity:player>process:game-client>launch-and-play`.

claims.title: Unverified matchmaking transport may reveal player match assignments
claims.description: `flow:process:game-client>process:lobby>matchmaking` crosses from `boundary:player-local-machine` to `boundary:production-network`, carries matchmaking requests and match assignments, and has `encryption_in_transit: unknown`. If the unverified TCP 1234 transport is not protected, an observer on the client-to-lobby path can intercept those requests and assignments. This is conditional on the unknown encryption state, not an assertion of plaintext. The collected assignments expose player activity and match composition, enabling targeted tracking or later attacks against identified matches.

quotes.text: The two client links are just port numbers.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because the flow crosses from player-controlled devices into production and its transport protection is unknown; impact is low because the stated content is matchmaking activity and assignments rather than a tagged sensitive-data corpus.

mitigations.summary: Encrypt and authenticate the matchmaking channel
mitigations.detail: Use TLS 1.2+ for TCP 1234, validate the lobby identity in the client, and set `encryption_in_transit` on `flow:process:game-client>process:lobby>matchmaking` to a verified protected state.
Use opaque match references and avoid placing unnecessary player identifiers in matchmaking messages.

claims.title: Unverified gameplay transport may expose match state to network observers
claims.description: `flow:process:game-client>process:game-server>gameplay-traffic` crosses from `boundary:player-local-machine` to `boundary:production-network` and carries gameplay actions and state updates, while `encryption_in_transit` is unknown. If that unverified TCP 1235 channel is not encrypted, an on-path observer can intercept live game state exchanged with `process:game-server`. This is conditional on the unknown protection state. Captured state can reveal game activity and operationally valuable match information, enabling targeted observation or abuse of match knowledge.

quotes.text: The two client links are just port numbers.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because the player-to-production flow crosses a trust boundary and its encryption is unknown; impact is medium because `process:game-server` handles `business-critical-data` and an observer can collect live match state from affected sessions.

mitigations.detail: Protect TCP 1235 with TLS or an authenticated encrypted game transport, validate peer identities, and record the verified `encryption_in_transit` state on `flow:process:game-client>process:game-server>gameplay-traffic`.

claims.title: Unverified lobby-to-game-server handoff may disclose player identifiers
claims.description: `flow:process:lobby>process:game-server>hand-over-match` carries match composition and player identifiers, but its `encryption_in_transit` attribute is unknown. If the production-network handoff lacks transport encryption, a compromised host or network observer on that internal path can intercept player identifiers and match composition. This is conditional on the unknown control state; it does not claim the internal link is plaintext. The identifiers can then be correlated with live match activity handled by `process:game-server`, improving targeting of particular players.

quotes.text: The lobby reads the player database to set up a match, and hands the match over to the game servers.

severity.justification: Likelihood is low and conditional because an attacker needs an internal production-network observation position and the handoff encryption state is unknown; impact is medium because the flow carries player identifiers into a `business-critical-data` game-server process.

mitigations.detail: Use mutually authenticated TLS between `process:lobby` and `process:game-server` and explicitly record the transport protection on `flow:process:lobby>process:game-server>hand-over-match`.
Pass opaque player and match references where the game server can resolve them through an authorized service path.

claims.title: Unverified lobby database transport may expose player account records
claims.description: `flow:process:lobby>store:player-database>read-players` reads player account records from `store:player-database`, whose assets include `pii`, and the flow's `encryption_in_transit` is unknown. If the unverified database connection is unencrypted, an observer on the production-network path can intercept account records as `process:lobby` reads them to form matches. This is conditional on the unknown transport state. The disclosure can reveal player records and provide identifiers that support targeting players through the lobby or moderation workflows.

quotes.text: The lobby reads the player database to set up a match

severity.justification: Likelihood is low and conditional because interception requires a production-network position and the database-flow encryption state is unknown; impact is high because `store:player-database` holds `pii` and the lobby read path can expose player account records in bulk.

mitigations.detail: Require TLS with server identity validation, preferably mTLS, for `flow:process:lobby>store:player-database>read-players`.
Restrict the lobby query and response to the minimum match-formation fields so the read path does not carry full player account records.

claims.title: Unverified game-server statistics transport may expose match statistics
claims.description: `flow:process:game-server>store:stats-database>read-write-stats` carries match statistics between `process:game-server` and `store:stats-database`, and `encryption_in_transit` is unknown. If the database connection is not encrypted, an observer with a production-network position can intercept match statistics in transit. This is conditional on the unknown transport control. The information can reveal match performance and operational game data, enabling targeted analysis of players or game behavior.

quotes.text: The game servers read and write the stats database during and after a match

severity.justification: Likelihood is low and conditional because the attacker needs a production-network observation position and the connection encryption is unknown; impact is medium because the flow and `store:stats-database` carry `business-critical-data`.

mitigations.summary: Require TLS for statistics database traffic
mitigations.detail: Configure authenticated TLS for `flow:process:game-server>store:stats-database>read-write-stats` and verify it is enforced for all database sessions.

claims.title: Unverified game-server player-record updates may disclose player data
claims.description: `flow:process:game-server>store:player-database>update-players` carries player progression and match results to `store:player-database`, which holds `pii` and `business-critical-data`, while `encryption_in_transit` is unknown. If the database transport is unencrypted, a production-network observer can intercept player progression and match-result updates. This is conditional on the unknown transport state. Captured identifiers and progression data can be correlated with account records and used to target particular players through downstream player-account workflows.

quotes.text: they also write back to the player database.

severity.justification: Likelihood is low and conditional because the attacker must observe a production-network database path and encryption is unknown; impact is high because the affected store is tagged `pii` and `business-critical-data` and receives player-linked results.

mitigations.detail: Enforce TLS or mTLS for `flow:process:game-server>store:player-database>update-players` and reject non-encrypted database sessions.
Send only the player reference and required progression delta rather than broader account data.

claims.title: Unverified support-to-moderation transport may expose player-account activity
claims.description: `flow:entity:customer-support-staff>process:moderation-website>moderate-accounts` crosses from `boundary:corporate-network` into `boundary:production-network`, carries moderation actions on player accounts, and has `encryption_in_transit: unknown`. If that unverified channel lacks encryption, an observer on the corporate-to-production path can intercept staff actions and player-account-related information. This is conditional on the unknown protection state. The disclosure can reveal sensitive moderation activity and identifiers that can be used to target player accounts or support personnel.

quotes.text: our customer support staff work from the corporate network and use a moderation website to look at and act on player accounts.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because the corporate-to-production flow crosses a trust boundary and lacks verified encryption; impact is medium because `process:moderation-website` and its support flow handle `pii` associated with player accounts.

mitigations.detail: Require TLS 1.2+ with strict certificate validation for `flow:entity:customer-support-staff>process:moderation-website>moderate-accounts`, and ensure corporate proxies do not log sensitive request content.
Use opaque account references and avoid placing player personal data in URLs, query strings, or client-visible diagnostic content.

claims.title: Unverified moderation database transport may expose player records
claims.description: `flow:process:moderation-website>store:player-database>read-write-players` directly reads player account records and moderation state from `store:player-database`; the flow carries `pii` and its `encryption_in_transit` is unknown. If the database connection is not encrypted, an observer on the production-network path can intercept player records and moderation state as the website accesses them. quotes.text: That website reads and writes the player database directly.

severity.justification: Likelihood is low and conditional because a production-network observation position is required and database-flow encryption is unknown; impact is high because `store:player-database` contains `pii` and the flow returns player account records and moderation state.

mitigations.detail: Require authenticated TLS for `flow:process:moderation-website>store:player-database>read-write-players` and prohibit plaintext database connections.
Limit the moderation website's queries and responses to the player fields necessary for the specific support task.

claims.title: A storage copy may expose all player records if player-database encryption at rest is absent
claims.description: `store:player-database` holds `pii` and `business-critical-data`, but its `encryption_at_rest` attribute is unknown. If that unknown resolves to storage without encryption at rest, an attacker who obtains a disk, snapshot, backup, or decommissioned storage copy can read player accounts directly without authenticating through the lobby, game server, or moderation website. This is conditional on the unverified at-rest control and does not claim the store is unencrypted. One copied artifact can expose the player corpus and supply identifiers for targeting activity through `process:lobby` and `process:moderation-website`.

quotes.text: The diagram doesn't record what authentication is on any of these links, or how any of the stores are protected.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because the encryption-at-rest posture is unknown and storage copies can be obtained outside the application path; impact is high because `store:player-database` contains the player corpus tagged `pii` and `business-critical-data`.

mitigations.summary: Verify and enforce encryption at rest for player records
mitigations.detail: Establish the encryption posture of `store:player-database`, then use managed envelope encryption with protected keys for the primary store and every backup, snapshot, replica, and export.
Limit snapshot, backup, and export permissions to dedicated roles and audit every copy operation.

mitigations.detail: Establish whether `store:stats-database` is encrypted at rest, then require managed-key encryption for the store and all operational copies.

claims.title: Code in a player-database reader may disclose the player corpus through its existing access
claims.description: `process:lobby` reads `store:player-database` through `flow:process:lobby>store:player-database>read-players`, and `process:moderation-website` reads it through `flow:process:moderation-website>store:player-database>read-write-players`; authentication on both database flows is unknown. If either reader has broader database read authority than its required fields and rows, an attacker who runs code in that reader can use its existing session or credentials to read player account records from `store:player-database`. This is conditional on the unverified access scope, not an assertion that authorization is absent. Such a read can expose the PII corpus and moderation state, then support targeted actions through the lobby and support workflows; encryption at rest would not stop a reader the database already authorizes.

quotes.text: The lobby reads the player database to set up a match
That website reads and writes the player database directly.

Audit and alert on bulk or unusual player-record reads by both service identities, including access outside expected matchmaking or moderation workflows.

claims.title: Code in the game server may disclose match statistics through its existing database access
claims.description: `process:game-server` accesses `store:stats-database` through `flow:process:game-server>store:stats-database>read-write-stats`, and authentication on that database flow is unknown. If the game-server database identity can read more statistics than a particular match operation requires, an attacker running code in `process:game-server` can use that established access to read accumulated statistics from `store:stats-database`. This is conditional on the unverified authentication and grant scope. The disclosure exposes historical match data and can provide game intelligence beyond the attacker’s own session; encryption at rest would not prevent reads made through the authorized service connection.

quotes.text: The game servers read and write the stats database during and after a match

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because `process:game-server` is internet-facing and its statistics-database authentication and authorization scope are unknown; impact is medium because `store:stats-database` contains accumulated `business-critical-data`.
